touches.text: Trouble: it has to be able to report when nothing else can, so a direct line makes sense for recovery (6.3.4).
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
A second observation of an open trouble NEVER issues a new ticket; it increments a counter on the open one.
Disposable once closed. File artifacts in the logging tree, cleared on the 30 day cycle by the cairn device during sleep (4.3.2.4).
The test before raising one: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble. One problem, one trouble.
They live inside the Recovery device (6.3.4), since recovery has to work when other things don't.

Transient things may help debugging out to 30 days and won't be needed past that, eg an inference ticket looked at a week later because a bug turned up. No trouble should stand unresolved at 30 days; sleep's cleanup may be made to spare one that does.
If the device won't come up, the shim retries; after many retries it files a trouble ticket for Akien and CC. This holds for every wake: a request, a pulse, the sleep token.
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.
Logging and diagnostics, including diagnostic_inspector: the smart reader of the dumb breadcrumbs base's logging leaves; complete diagnosis on the first pass.

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).
intentions_model_compiler: copies every intention into intentions-congruency-lab/. WHY: so that one folder can regrow the system on a bare machine. USERS: Cairn (cairn compile).

open_questions.text: The harbor's bus face also answers `clear`: the crossing gate's door (clearance.py), which codemother's `cross` verb already asks, and which CC's cross helper would ask instead of importing clearance (RULE 1, ticket 5e11fadd63b3). You said 2026-10-17 it houses the gates "only because we had to have some place to put them". Is `clear` a harbor verb to add here, or should a crossing reach the gate through another door?

Route also moves a domain's preferred models ahead of cheaper ones (route.py:301, since 2026-08-28), and nothing here names that. Does the walk order read "a domain's preferred models first, then cheapest", or does the preference go?
